function: Joint fluid-antenna port selection and opportunistic scheduling at each UE, under partial SINR observation, to maximize downlink sum-rate in opportunistic FAMA (pp. 1-2).
system: Downlink: BS with M fixed antennas (one per UE, no precoding); each UE has a K-port linear fluid antenna, one port active; no RIS; band unstated (pp. 1-3).
method: Partially observable mean-field multi-agent actor-critic (MFAC): decentralized UE agents with fully connected actor and critic networks (1024-512-256-128, ReLU, Adam); reinforcement learning (pp. 2-4).
data_channel: Custom simulation: Rayleigh fading with Jakes (J0) spatial correlation among fluid-antenna ports; distances and path loss omitted; the only channel model used (p. 2).
test_conditions: Default K=100, M=6, W=2, |P|=30, 400 episodes; training runs shown per M (Fig. 2, Table I); sum-rate swept over M=3-10, K=30-100, W=1-5 (pp. 4-5).
baselines: Learned: MA SD3-DerivNet [17], multi-agent RL with dual policy networks and derivative-based reward shaping. Non-learned: exhaustive search over all action combinations, the optimal upper bound (pp. 1, 4).
metrics: Sum-rate (bit/s/Hz) versus number of UEs, ports, and fluid-antenna size; normalized sum capability per episode (convergence); training time in seconds (pp. 4-5).
complexity: Critic complexity O((|Su|+2|Au|)h1+sum_i(hi*hi+1)+hI), independent of M, versus O((|Su|+M|Au|)h1+...) for traditional actor-critic (p. 3); training time 405-662 s versus 9600-12800 s for MA SD3-DerivNet, M=3-5 (p. 4).
q1_support: p. 2: "We assume that all channels follow a Rayleigh distribution", with port correlation from "the classical Jake's model". Custom simulator; no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO, or measured channel.
q2_support: p. 4: "Table I shows the training time of the proposed approach and MA SD3-DerivNet under different number of UEs". Training is run per number of UEs (also Fig. 2); Figs. 3-5 sweep M, K, W, but no trained model is stated to be tested in an unseen configuration.
q3_support: p. 4: "We compare the proposed approach with (1) the MA SD3-DerivNet scheme proposed in [17] ... and (2) exhaustive search". Earlier learned O-FAMA RL method and non-learned optimum, both compared on sum-rate in Figs. 3-5 (pp. 4-5).
q4_support: p. 3: "Then the complexity of our approach can be expressed as O((|Su| + 2|Au|)h1^critic + sum_{i=2}^{I-1} hi^critic hi+1^critic + hI^critic)"; p. 4, Table I: training time "405s 542s 662s" for M = 3, 4, 5.
q5_support: p. 2: "We assume that all channels follow a Rayleigh distribution". Channels are simulated; the paper gives no code or data link and uses no public channel dataset or measured data.
notes: The PDF is the preprint (LaTeX template header, five authors); Crossref gives the same title in IEEE Communications Letters with seven authors, so it is the paper of the DOI. Eligibility: the learned action joins fluid-antenna port selection (physical layer) with opportunistic UE scheduling (above it), so it passes above_phy by the joint rule. Area 3 is a judgment for the reviewer to confirm: port selection is a one-hot receive-side spatial configuration (p. 3) that replaces precoding for interference rejection (p. 1), akin to antenna or beam selection, but it is not literally a BS precoder, beam, or RIS phase shift; read narrowly, area 3 would not fit and the work would be excluded with reason function (p. 1). The system check passes: multi-antenna BS (p. 1) and a K-port fluid antenna at each UE (p. 2). q3: the non-learned comparison is the exhaustive-search optimum used as upper bound (p. 4). q4: order of complexity of the critic (p. 3) and measured training time (Table I, p. 4). Equations on pp. 2-3 were checked against the page images because the text extraction garbles them.
